questions.q: What is the default ON_ERROR behavior in COPY INTO?
options: ABORT_STATEMENT — any error fails the whole file's load
CONTINUE — bad rows are silently skipped
SKIP_FILE — the entire file is always skipped on any error
There is no default; ON_ERROR must always be specified
questions.explain: ABORT_STATEMENT is the default so that errors are loud and noticed, rather than silently dropping rows.

options: Parses the file and reports every row that would fail, without loading any rows into the table
Loads all valid rows and deletes the invalid ones afterward
Automatically fixes malformed rows before loading them
Disables ON_ERROR checking entirely
questions.explain: VALIDATION_MODE is a dry run — it reports what would fail without committing any rows to the target table.

questions.q: Why does ON_ERROR = 'CONTINUE' require a deliberate decision rather than being a safe default?
options: It can silently drop rows without anyone noticing, unlike the loud failure of ABORT_STATEMENT
It always loads duplicate rows
It disables the file format entirely
It only works with internal stages
questions.explain: CONTINUE skips bad rows quietly — useful when chosen deliberately, but risky as an unexamined default since data loss can go unnoticed.

questions.q: What two arguments does the COPY_HISTORY table function require?
options: A table name and a time window
A warehouse name and a role
A file format name and a stage name
A database name and a schema name
questions.explain: COPY_HISTORY is a table function (not a static view) that requires TABLE_NAME and a START_TIME window, keeping it fast even on large accounts.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does this lesson use only code cards and no screenshot?
options: No real Snowsight screenshot for ON_ERROR/VALIDATION_MODE/load-history topics was found on quickstarts.snowflake.com or docs.snowflake.com after checking
Screenshots are against course policy for every lesson

The images were too large to embed
